sentences.text: The name Troodon means "wounding tooth" in Ancient Greek, referring to the unique serrations on its teeth. These teeth have prominent ridges oriented apically, a feature distinct from other theropods. Based on the model Stenonychosaurus, the animal had a long neck, long narrow jaws with small sharp teeth, short forelimbs with three clawed fingers, and long hind legs adapted for running. It possessed long upper limbs that it folded against the chest wall like a bird. The animal measured approximately 2 meters in length, 1 meter in height, and weighed between 27 and 45 kilograms. It possessed large sickle-shaped retractable claws on the second toe of each foot, which were raised off the ground when running.

Researchers suggest that Troodon practiced communal nesting, where multiple females laid eggs together at a single site to form large clutches due to limited individual egg production. Troodon eggs were characterized by a steep inclination, a trait distinct from both birds and crocodilians. Similar to crocodilian eggs, Troodon eggs were not rotated and were lightly buried in the nest.

The type species Troodon formosus was discovered in October 1855 and was initially mistaken for a lizard until 1877. Troodon formosus was discovered in 1855 and is one of the first dinosaurs found in North America and Asia. The genus Troodon was named by Leidy in 1856.

The tooth serrations of Troodon are morphometrically similar to those of herbivorous reptiles, suggesting it may have had an omnivorous diet. Research hypothesizes that the primary diet of Troodon consisted of meat. The morphology of Troodon's teeth is more similar to that of herbivorous reptiles, suggesting an omnivorous diet. It was proposed that wear patterns on all Troodon teeth suggest a diet based on soft foods, ruling out the consumption of bones, invertebrate exoskeletons, or hard plant matter.

Studies of teeth from northern Alaska suggest that northern populations of Troodon grew to a larger average body size than southern populations, hinting at Bergmann's rule. A study of multiple Troodon teeth found in Upper Cretaceous deposits in northern Alaska found them much larger than those from southern localities, providing evidence that Alaskan populations reached a larger body size. The study suggests Alaskan Troodon may have preyed on large animals because that habitat likely lacked large tyrannosaurs to compete for resources.

Troodon is considered a nomen dubium because its holotype consists of only a single tooth. Troodon has historically been an unstable classification and has been subject to numerous conflicting synonymies with similar theropod specimens.
